passage: I work at the next desk to Sumit, so I saw this unfold. In March, Sumit's mother Urmila called every night from home, and one evening Sumit put the phone down and rubbed both eyes. "She wants me to quit and move back," Sumit said. "She says it's my responsibility. I love her. I also just got this promotion." I didn't know what to say. A week later Sumit brought a piece of paper to lunch: the mother would spend half the year with Sumit's aunt, and half in Pune with Sumit; a neighbour would drop in daily, and Sumit would go home once a month. "I told her honestly what I can and can't do," Sumit said. I can't say how it felt for Sumit, but the calls after that got shorter and warmer.

qa.q: In which month did Urmila start calling every night?
What might Sumit be feeling about the mother's request, judging from Sumit's words?
qa.a: Love and pressure at once: Sumit says Sumit loves her but has just got a promotion, and rubbed both eyes after the call.

qa.q: What arrangement did Sumit work out, and why is it reasonable?
qa.a: The mother would spend half the year with the aunt and half in Pune with Sumit, a neighbour would drop in daily and Sumit would visit monthly, so it honours her needs and Sumit's life.

qa.q: How might Urmila have felt when Sumit said honestly what Sumit could and couldn't do?
qa.a: Urmila may have been disappointed at first, but the plan still kept her cared for and close to Sumit. The calls after that got shorter and warmer, which suggests she felt reassured.

grounding: Shows a parent expecting the protagonist to give up job, city or plans and calling it duty, the protagonist feeling love and pressure, finding arrangements that honour both and speaking honestly about limits, seen by an observer.
